issue_paraphrase: The RIBES machine-translation quality metric crashes with a ZeroDivisionError when the candidate translation is empty, when the list of references for a sentence is empty, or when the entire corpus is empty: the scoring code divides by the hypothesis token count and by the number of reference sets without guarding against zero. Empty inputs should simply yield a score of 0.0, and reference/hypothesis lists of unequal length should be rejected with a clear error instead of silently mis-scoring.
fix_summary: sentence_ribes now returns 0.0 when references or hypothesis is empty; corpus_ribes raises ValueError on mismatched reference/hypothesis list lengths and returns 0.0 for an empty corpus.
notes: Pure function, no corpus data or network needed. Test file already exists at parent (the fix only appends tests), so no test-file checkout is needed for the parent direction.

issue_paraphrase: Converting a parse tree to Chomsky normal form crashes whenever an internal node with more than two children has at least one plain terminal among its children (a word, a punctuation mark such as '+', or even a non-string value like an integer) sitting alongside full subtrees. The binarization step assumes every child is a subtree and reads a label from it, raising an AttributeError. Terminals should be treated as leaf nodes and their own string value carried into the intermediate node names.
fix_summary: chomsky_normal_form now builds childNodes with str(child.label()) for Tree children and str(child) for plain terminals, so mixed terminal/subtree nodes binarize instead of crashing; str() also handles non-string terminals.
notes: Pure tree transformation, no data or network. The test file exists at parent (the fix modifies it in place), so the parent direction only needs the source tree at parent. The underlying request is old upstream issue #1883; never name that number in instruction.md.

issue_paraphrase: Parsing trees in standard labeled-bracket notation fails whenever a leaf or label contains a parenthesis escaped with a backslash - for example a smiley ':)' written as ':\)' or a literal '(' written as '\(\('. The parser raises a ValueError about an unexpected parenthesis or unexpected end-of-string, and even partially-parseable inputs never round-trip: printing the tree does not reproduce the original string. Backslash-escaped brackets should be treated as literal characters and preserved exactly.
fix_summary: The fromstring tokenizer regex now accepts a backslash-escaped opening/closing bracket as a single verbatim token character (token_char = backslash-bracket or any char that is not whitespace/bracket), so escaped brackets parse as literal leaves/labels instead of being confused with structural brackets; the existing str() escaping already handled output.
notes: CAUTION: nltk/test/unit/test_tree.py is a NEW file in the fix commit; when checking the buggy parent use 'git reset --hard <parent> && git clean -fd && git checkout <fix> -- nltk/test/unit/test_tree.py' and never a bare 'git checkout .' afterwards (it would silently restore the staged fix). No data or network needed.

issue_paraphrase: Tokenizing text that starts with a single-quoted multi-letter word (for example 'Hard' or 'hello') leaves the opening quote glued to the word, producing tokens like "'Hard" instead of a separate quote token, and for words that happen to match a short pattern (as in 'tis) the word itself is split in two. Words with intra-word apostrophes such as o'clock or O'Connor must stay intact. The tokenizer should separate an opening single quote whenever it is followed by a word, without disturbing clitic contractions like 're or 's.
fix_summary: Replaced the opening-quote padding regex '(\')(?!re|ve|ll|m|t|s|d|n)(\w)\b' (which only fired before single-letter words) with '(?<!\w)(\')(?!(?:re|ve|ll|m|t|s|d|n)\b)(?=\w)', a lookbehind/lookahead form that pads the quote before any word while the clitic lookahead and the (?<!\w) guard keep contractions and intra-word apostrophes untouched.
notes: Direct repro via NLTKWordTokenizer needs no data. The project's regression test calls word_tokenize, which needs nltk.download('punkt_tab') (small download; trials have egress) - either pre-seed it in the task image or use the direct repro as the oracle. The one unrelated tokenize failure (test_legality_principle_syllable_tokenizer, needs another punkt model) should be excluded from any full-file run.
